_doc: Scripted user turns for DESIGN-live-test.md. Each turn is one `claude -p` call resuming the same session. `role` tags what the turn is for in scoring: constraint (states the early constraint), chore, finished (the turn ends a finished step: an offer after it is allowed), midtask (the turn lands mid-chore or mid-investigation: an offer after it is a harm), oneshot (a one-shot question: an offer after it is a harm), investigation (S2: its tokens are the benefit endpoint), fix (S2: its result is checked by hidden/check.py). `decline` is prepended to the next turn when the previous reply offered a fresh start: `first` for the first offer, `again` for every later one. S2's chore turns run single test modules, never tests/test_sync.py, tests/test_export.py or tests/test_limits.py, so the flaky tests first appear in the investigation. `overlay` names a folder copied over fixture/ for that scenario only; with it, the CI logs are eight real runs of the working copy's suite (S2-REDESIGN.md). S2's investigation (t6, t7) asks about a long chat thread in the overlay, docs/incidents/flaky-ci-thread.md, whose agreed fix is stated only late and by reference (S2-PROSE.md). S3 (the no-re-offer test, NO-REOFFER-DESIGN.md) reuses S1's fixture and chores: at t6 the user asks whether a fresh session would be better, and t7 declines whatever the reply was (`decline_in_text`: the turn's own text carries the decline, so run.py adds no prefix to it and treats it as the first decline).
